question.question: A fair six-sided die is rolled repeatedly until the first 6 appears. Given that the first 6 occurs on an even-numbered roll, what is the probability that it occurs on roll 2? Give the exact fraction first and a brief explanation.
question.incorrect_argument: Once we know the first 6 occurs on an even roll, the eligible rolls are 2, 4, 6 and so on. Each eligible roll has a 1/6 chance of being a 6, so the probability that the first eligible roll is the successful one remains 1/6.
question.correct_explanation: The probability that the first 6 occurs on roll 2 is (5/6)(1/6). The probability that it occurs on any even roll is the geometric sum (5/36)/(1-25/36) = 5/11. The conditional probability is therefore (5/36)/(5/11) = 11/36.
